backbone_atoms.note: Binder mode writes a C-alpha trace and no N, C or O. This is the pairing the guard exists for. The declaration covers binder mode, which is the only mode a binder campaign runs. Genie3 returns the target as a C-alpha trace as well, so no stage downstream of this one recovers the target's sidechains from the generator's output. Genie3 also relabels chains. The measured run handed it a target on chain A and got that target back on chain B, with the generated binder on chain A. A campaign that excludes its target by chain letter therefore excludes the binder whenever the target is chain A. What Genie3 reads from a target is conditional on which of the target's residues are interface residues, and this field holds a flat list, so requires stays unknown rather than hold a value that is wrong for one of the two cases.

At the pinned revision aqlaboratory/genie3@5214459c42e69b01fadfc7d7ebda09d8e5082115, src/genie3/generation/utils/feat_utils.py appends residue.atom_type[1:2], the C-alpha slot, for every target residue, and additionally appends residue.atom_type[4:], the sidechain heavy atoms from CB outward, only for residues the atomize mask selects. For a target chain that mask is the interface-residue mask, and it is forced to all zeros when the representation mode is Calpha. N, C and O are never taken: the token count the code computes is the residue's atom count less three, commented there as excluding C, N and O. So the requirement is C-alpha for every target residue plus sidechain heavy atoms for interface residues, which a flat list cannot express. Settled by: vendoring the pinned feat_utils.py under this repository, or a backbone_atoms schema that can hold a conditional requirement.

The upstream ships bindcraft fetch-weights for exactly that case, describing it as what a compute node with no route to the internet needs run for it on a login node first. A first run with no parameters present downloads 5.3 GB instead, which is setup rather than job-time traffic, and the adapter's toolcheck reports a missing parameter set as a named missing input rather than fetching it. The optional HTML trajectory viewer loads a 3Dmol.js dependency from the network when someone opens it, which is a viewing concern and not a job-time one.
